messages:
maria: Quick q — how should we treat pre-release identifiers and +build metadata for semver bumps? Example: we have 1.4.2+meta. Build metadata only shouldn't change precedence but should we force a patch bump when metadata changes? I'm worried releasebot auto-skip logic will treat +build as no-op.

jon: My take: +build is metadata — semver says it doesn't affect precedence, so no patch required for pure metadata. But release pipelines often need a new artifact id.

sam: Agreed. For deploybot/deploy workflow, we need unique artifacts to avoid caching. Could tag with an -meta.<hash> prerelease? e.g., 1.4.2-meta.20240215

maria: That would be a prerelease, not strictly metadata. Do we want deploybot to accept prereleases for prod? :thinking: 

alice: I'd rather keep prod releases stable (no prerelease). Option: leave semver 1.4.2 and append buildmeta in CI artifact name (not package tag) so dependency managers don't treat it as different.

jon: Good call. But release-notes-bot expects version strings — if CI artifact != package version, release notes may become noisy.

release-notes-bot: automated: if artifact_name != package_version then note appended under 'buildmeta' in release notes. :gear:

sam: For deploy-bot: can we make it prefer package_version for routing but fall back to artifact hash for cache-busting? e.g., routing key: 1.4.2 (artifact: 1.4.2+ci.abc123)

deploy-bot: automated: routing policy updated in draft. New behavior: allow +build on artifact names for uniqueness; routing canonicalizes on version core+prerelease (ignore +build) unless explicit --force-hash flag.

maria: Nice. So policy: no semver bump for +build-only changes; artifact gets +ci.<hash>; releasebot/release-notes include buildmeta section; deploy-bot canonicalizes. I'll update the RFC and docs. Thanks all. :tada:
